name: R22 C3 fixed-checkpoint readout mechanism diagnostic
label: PILOT/DEVELOPMENT
theory_unchanged: J=EP[T]-EQ[T]-.5EP[T^2]-.5EQ[T^2]; at optimum T*=(p-q)/(p+q). No new variational claim.

readouts.PMI_C2: mean clip(2*atanh(clip(T,+/-(1-1e-4))),-2,2), per-position clipping before mean

selection: Historical J-selected checkpoint for every unit. No new checkpoint or threshold selection. CAL descriptive only.

questions.PMI_C2-PMI: Does limiting extreme per-position scores help, especially BF loose success?
questions.POS-J: Effect of removing the negative/reference first and second moments.
questions.EPT-POS: Effect of additionally removing the positive second moment.
questions.PMI-EPT: Effect of the inverse-tanh transform at otherwise positive-only scoring.
questions.VCS-InfoNCE: Same readout comparison plus clipping-gain difference; shared gains do not establish VCS-specific advantage.

primary_endpoints.bf: PMI_C2-PMI success<42; report success<9 simultaneously, no hiding a tradeoff
primary_endpoints.epfl: PMI_C2-J scene-macro success<2.25 native px; report <10.5 simultaneously

report: All five readouts, all three seeds, paired flips, median errors and scene/core bootstrap 10000 resamples at seed20261022. No selecting winning arm after DEV. Intervals condition on trained seeds.
limitations: Existing trained families have recipe differences; this is not objective-only retraining.
Tanh parameterization alone does not establish PMI calibration.
Clipped PMI is a heuristic application readout, not the unchanged theorem objective.
Same-job pairing retains GPU search nondeterminism.
_publication_note: Public scientific protocol excerpt; not an operational freeze, source manifest or admission authorization.
